definitions.explanation: A person who enters a place without permission or authorization. Can refer to burglars, unauthorized visitors, or in a broader sense, foreign invaders.

examples.japanese: {侵入者|しんにゅうしゃ}が{捕|つか}まった。
セキュリティカメラに{侵入者|しんにゅうしゃ}が{映|うつ}っていた。
examples.english: An intruder was captured on the security camera.

examples.japanese: {夜中|よなか}に{侵入者|しんにゅうしゃ}が{庭|にわ}に{入|はい}ってきたので、すぐに{警察|けいさつ}に{通報|つうほう}した。
examples.english: An intruder came into the yard in the middle of the night, so I immediately called the police.

notes:
Composed of {侵入|しんにゅう} (intrusion, trespassing) + {者|しゃ} (person). The word carries a clear negative connotation — the person is somewhere they should not be.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {侵入者|しんにゅうしゃ}を{捕|つか}まえる — to catch an intruder
- {侵入者|しんにゅうしゃ}を{検知|けんち}する — to detect an intruder
- {不法|ふほう}{侵入者|しんにゅうしゃ} — illegal trespasser

RELATED TERMS:
- {侵入|しんにゅう} — intrusion, trespassing (the act itself)
- {不審者|ふしんしゃ} — suspicious person; broader term, not necessarily someone who has already entered
- {泥棒|どろぼう} — thief, burglar; implies intent to steal
